about: The vocabulary of reasons for choosing a play, built from the player's own words during play. Claude tags each explained play with these codes (catalog/annotations.jsonl). A new code starts as 'proposed' and becomes 'adopted' only when the player agrees; its definition uses the player's words.

reasons.name: Uncover the most hidden
reasons.definition: My normal goal is to uncover face-down cards on the column with the most face-down cards. The overarching strategy is to uncover the card on the columns that has the most potential to reveal more cards to be played.

history.name: Uncover the most hidden
history.definition: My normal goal is to uncover face-down cards on the column with the most face-down cards.

reasons.name: Right-most playable first
reasons.definition: At the beginning of the game, I do this by selecting the right-most card that is playable.

reasons.name: Automatic home play
reasons.definition: An ace always goes straight to home since not playing it has the most downside (covering a face-down card, blocking a column from accepting a high card, preventing the next card in the home pile from being played, etc.). Moving an ace to home has only upside consequences. When more than one ace can go home, both aces will be played before any other play, so the order in which they're played is of no material consequence. When the ace of a suit is on the foundation and the two becomes playable, it is an automatic play because there is absolutely no progressive play value to leaving it unplayed. Likewise, since 2♥ and AT LEAST 2♦ have been played to home, playing 3♠ to home (on 2♠) is automatic: there is no progressive-play reason not to play it.

reasons.name: Keep options open
reasons.definition: I don't want to make that decision prematurely. Not playing either of them until I have a king to put in the columns is an unnecessary decision that locks me into a position before I know what's coming next. Leaving them in place leaves my options open.

reasons.name: Only new plays
reasons.definition: No new play, so I'll draw ("NNP"; earlier "NNM", changed to be consistent with my preferred use of the word "play" instead of "move"). / The 7♦w-a is the only new play, so I'll play it. / Moving a run from one card to a matching card is only a "useful" play when freeing up the card that the moved card is blocking becomes immediately playable.

history.name: Only new plays
history.definition: No new play, so I'll draw. / The 7♦w-a is the only new play, so I'll play it.

history.name: Only new plays
history.definition: No new play, so I'll draw. / The 7♦w-a is the only new play, so I'll play it. / Moving a run from one card to a matching card is only a "useful" play when freeing up the card that the moved card is blocking becomes immediately playable.

reasons.name: Build the longer run
reasons.definition: When there is nothing else to consider, I play the 9 with the most run-cards on it. There may be no advantage in doing so, but I opt for continuing to build an existing longer run over starting or adding to a smaller one (all other things being equal).

reasons.name: King to an empty column
reasons.definition: Because my goal is to not use memory/card-counting, playing a king is an automatic play, similar to the reason for always playing an ace on its home pile.

reasons.name: Seen this pass
reasons.definition: A card's progressive play value, judged by what I've seen in the current turn of the waste pile: e.g. playing 6♥ revealed 6♦, which I mentally note as potentially of no new progressive play value since I've not seen a black 5 in the current turn of the waste pile.

reasons.name: Keep a target
reasons.definition: Hold a card back from home when it can take a card I may want to play later: if the 3♣ becomes playable, it can be played on the 4♦. At this point in the game, the potential for a future play of 3♣ outweighs the relatively benign current move of 4♦ to home.

reasons.name: Home pace by colour
reasons.definition: As a general rule, I try not to play a card to home if it is more than two ranks higher than the lowest card of the opposite color currently played to a home pile. A suit whose ace hasn't been played counts as 0 (e.g. 0♣).

reasons.name: Left-most target
reasons.definition: I consider both plays as essentially neutral unless there is a clear reason to leave one or the other open. As such, by default, a card with multiple targets is played on the left-most target card.

reasons.name: Hoping for a card
reasons.definition: In my mind, I'm hoping to reveal a particular card soon so a play can follow: e.g. a black 4 so I can reveal a card on g, especially because the stock pile is dwindling.
